posts.author: Frogboy
posts.body:
I was toying around with the idea of creating some RPG Maker themed Memes ... and then I realized that I had no where to share them except for here. It's not like RPG Maker is pop culture enough to post them on Facebook or anything. I hope you'll join in and make some more to share.
The only rule I have for this thread is that all of the Memes need to be RPG Maker related (or at least strongly focused towards RPGs or Visual Novels). This is not a general, "post funny memes" thread as that's pretty much all Facebook is now a days and I have zero desire to see the same things here. This is to be specifically targeted for us (and mostly made by us as no one else would likely find these amusing anyway). So without further ado, here we go.

posts.author: XIIIthHarbinger
posts.body:
@JGreene
(shrugs)
I saw it, & thought it was a perfect representation of one of early balancing attempts.
Essentially, because my game is an open world sandbox, the player can potentially wander into the "wrong neighborhood", & get squished, or wander back through areas where they are "a god among insects". So to counter that to some extent I started using Yanfly's Enemy Level plugin, so that the enemy can scale with the player. I put my party up against a level one Vampire, (essentially an elite undead unit), who proceeded to one shot my entire party before a single one of them could even move.
I realized that in my adjustments, I had made certain enemies a little too powerful, especially at early levels.

posts.author: Poryg
posts.body:
@Oddball
Do your homework first. Definitely not Java
In fact while Java applets were a thing in the early 2000's, the only browser that really supported them was Firefox. In 2007 the popularity of Java applets faded greatly however as interwebs got its own language. The language that MV is using.
MV uses nwjs, which is based on Chromium. In fact the vast majority of the internet browsers is built on Chromium. And Chromium as we know it never really supported Java applets.
Not to mention, Java is a compiled language, which compiles into Java bytecode, which is then translated into machine code by Java virtual machine. This all means that it's not dynamic compared to the language MV is using. Also, it's very tedious to program in Java due to the kinda awful syntax of programming.

posts.author: Kes
Ksi
posts.body:
Sure thing~
The 3-tile rule was something that people came up with in the early-to-mid 2000s. It was a general guideline on how to map correctly. See, back then we didn't really care about the pretty - people were more preoccupied with creating cool systems and pushing the bounds of the engine, to see what they could make with eventing, even if it ended up being a jumbled mess. Stuff like pseudo 3D landscapes that you could move in, Custom Battle and Menu Systems, and a variety of other interesting stuff (banking systems with interest, party caterpillar systems, etc).
Because of the interest in only creating systems, a lot of the games back then suffered from huge empty areas and long straight lines. You'd be hard pressed to find a map with much decoration and those few that did appear were highly lauded. In an order to promote prettier maps (and thus, prettier games) it was suggested that people adhere to something called the 3-tile rule.
The rule boils down to this: every three tiles on the map there should be something to break up the ground tile.
Now the issue is that this led to people just throwing details down like they didn't care. There was no thought put into the addition of the tiles (or, little thought at least) and white/negative space suffered incredibly due to this.
The idea behind the rule was more for nature areas and to do mainly with cliff, water and tree-line tiles, though - to break up the straight lines that a lot of people fell in to when mapping those particular tiles. The confusion sprung from the fact that trees tended to count as plants and people used it for plants. But yeah, it got taken too far.

Too much:
